raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

I've got 13.1 mu to work with. Like most years, I split it — about **8 mu for wheat-maize double cropping** on the better land near the road, and the remaining **5.1 mu for cotton** on the plot that's a bit sandier and doesn't hold water as well. That's how my father did it and it's worked for me for 15 years. Cotton gives me cash in the fall, wheat-maize keeps the family fed and brings in steady income.

Our household is just 3 people and my wife does some work at the factory in the county town, so labor is tight. That's part of why I keep some cotton even though picking is hard work — the price is decent and I can hire a few neighbors during picking season if I need to. Maize and wheat I can mostly handle with the combine harvester service that comes through the village.

**On the wheat** (already planted last October, variety Jimai 22 like most folks around here): I put down compound fertilizer before planting — about 40 kg of 15-15-15 per mu plus maybe 10 kg of urea mixed in for the base. In spring at jointing I'll topdress another 15 kg of urea per mu. The extension guy says you don't need that much but I've seen the wheat go yellow when I cut back, so I stick with what works. I'll irrigate at returning-green, jointing, and grain-filling — 3 times is usually enough, 4 if it's really dry. Winter irrigation I did already in December. Herbicide once for the broadleaf weeds. Expecting maybe **450 kg/mu** — last year was 470 so I'm hoping for similar if the spring weather holds.

**On the maize** (DK958 or similar hybrid, planted right after wheat harvest in mid-June — we have maybe 5-7 days to turn the field around): I'll direct-seed into the wheat stubble with the planter, no tillage. Compound fertilizer at planting, about 35 kg/mu of 15-15-15 plus urea topdress at around the big trumpet stage — maybe 15 kg/mu of urea. Summer has rain usually so I only irrigate once or twice if July goes dry. Spray herbicide after planting and I watch for fall armyworm — that's been showing up more in recent years. Hoping for **500 kg/mu**, maize has been pretty steady.

**On the cotton** (5.1 mu): I'll plant in late April with film mulch like everyone around here. Cotton takes more work — spraying for bollworm and aphids 4-5 times through summer, and the picking is the hard part. We pick 3 times from September through October. I'll use about 12 kg N/mu total, less than wheat because cotton doesn't need as much and too much N makes it grow too tall with less boll set. I'll hire 2-3 people for maybe a week during peak picking since my wife can only help on weekends. Expecting **250 kg/mu of lint**. Cotton price last year was okay, I'm hoping it doesn't drop.

I try not to spend more than I have to on fertilizer — the prices went up again this year and the subsidy barely covers the difference. But I don't cut too much because a bad yield hurts worse than saving 50 yuan on fertilizer. That's just how it is.
